findings.reason: the plan fixes the wrong modules for the behaviour it declares, and a worker following it edits code the hold never passes through while the deferral at `queue_landing.py:2261` keeps firing.
findings.text: s22's "Write paths: reckon/crew/pending_landing.py, reckon/crew/resumption.py, reckon/crew/recovery_classification.py" omits both modules the described behaviour actually lives in: the hold is written, read and released in `reckon/crew/resume.py` (`hold_delivery` :155, `release_hold` :191, `hold_reason` :95, where a `released_at`-stamped hold still returns its reason because `hold_reason` never reads the release), and the pass that defers a held run is `reckon/crew/pending_landing.py`'s sibling `reckon/crew/queue_landing.py:2261` (`delivery_hold_reason` → `skipped.append({"status": "held"})`), so a node fenced to the named paths cannot make the release reach the lander

findings.reason: one of the deliverable's two release routes carries no arm, so the section's measure cannot show that route exists.
findings.text: s22's deliverable releases a resume's hold "when that attempt is judged, by review or by the run's own terminal manifest", but every arm measures only the review route (a reviewed-clean attempt, an attempt still running, a coordinator's own verb, §18's promoted run, and a manual release), so an implementation that releases the hold only when a review lands passes the whole case while the manifest route stays unimplemented

findings.reason: the queue-wide clause is a separate endpoint that, kept inside s22, is neither reviewed on its own nor measured on its own.
findings.text: s22 carries two rules of different reach: a run whose resume hold is judged is released (run-scoped, §22's title), and "A promoted run whose head is on the primary branch is retired as §18 states whatever hold it carries" (a rule that a hold never blocks §18's release at all, whatever set it), so one verdict cannot close both and the fourth fixture proves only the second

findings.reason: if the retained pointers came from §18's own refusal conditions rather than a hold, releasing resume holds leaves the costly symptom exactly where it was.
findings.text: s22's Why names the hold as the cause of the seven promoted runs keeping their live pointers, but the evidence it gives for those seven is "which only a discard retired", "20 MB of stored matches" and a monitor pass of 252 s → 69 s, none of which shows those runs carried holds, while §18's own `done` record (`plan.html:159`) names two other conditions under which nothing of such a run is removed (an unclean worktree, an unresolvable commit) that the same figures equally explain

findings.reason: an arm whose later attempt asks for help after a complete first attempt separates the declared newest-attempt rule from "complete always wins", which otherwise passes and would report a run as delivered while its live attempt waits for help.
findings.text: s23's deliverable is "a run's state is read from its newest attempt", but its single two-attempt fixture only tests help-request-then-complete, which an implementation that ranks a complete manifest above every later attempt also passes; the reverse ordering (a first attempt complete, a resumed attempt asking for help) is untested, so the plan's own rule and the cheaper rule are indistinguishable to this gate

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — §18 resolves at `plan.html:157`, and `reckon/crew/pending_landing.py`, `reckon/crew/resumption.py` and `reckon/crew/recovery_classification.py` all exist at the review revision `1c1aab83`; the two test files s22 and s23 name are deliverables, which is the house convention elsewhere in this plan.
rubric_items.done_when: two findings — s22's `plan.html:185` arms cover a reviewed-clean attempt but never the deliverable's second judgment route (the run's own terminal manifest), and s23's `plan.html:191` single fixture is passed by an implementation in which a complete manifest always outranks any later attempt.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — s22 and s23 send their gate evidence to named test files (`plan.html:185`, `plan.html:191`), not to a session scratchpad or a node-local temporary path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — both new sections name a behaviour ("a hold set for a resume", "a resumed run that finishes complete") and carry no plan label, stage name or ticket number into the symbols or test names they propose.
rubric_items.reasoning: two findings — s22's `plan.html:185` write paths name three modules the hold mechanism never passes through, and s22's `plan.html:183` attributes the seven retained pointers to a hold that its own figures do not show they carried.
rubric_items.single_goal: a finding — s22 at `plan.html:184` joins ending a resume's hold to a queue-wide rule that a hold never blocks §18's release, so its gate proves neither rule alone.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — `plan.html:24` lists `s22` and `s23` as upstream of `s10`, and each section presupposes only already-declared `done` sections (s22 the release at `plan.html:157`, s23 the classifier repairs), so neither has an unmet dependency; neither key has an entry of its own, which is a record gap that reorders nothing.
